verifications.note: "The 12-inch, 21-mile pipeline that tapped into the Alliance Pipeline northeast of Milnor and ran southwest to Gwinner has been serving natural gas to the Doosan Bobcat facility since September 2018."

resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded StartLocation=Milnor / EndLocation='Qwinner' (ND). This Wahpeton Daily News piece (already on this row for Diameter/Fuel/FuelSource/Length/Operator/PipelineType/Start/Status) states the route directly: the 12-inch, 21-mile line 'tapped into the Alliance Pipeline northeast of Milnor and ran southwest to Gwinner' -- confirming Milnor as the northeast/start end and Gwinner as the southwest/delivery end, and identifying the sheet's 'Qwinner' as a typo for Gwinner (both towns are named repeatedly and consistently throughout the article, dateline Wahpeton ND, and Gwinner is where the Doosan Bobcat plant itself sits). Single-source (medium tier): the two AP-wire pieces already on this row (pgjonline, and Washington Times via Wayback) name Gwinner as the delivery point but never mention Milnor or the route's other end, so they corroborate only half the Location pair and are wire-syndicate duplicates of each other besides. montana-dakota.com/about-us (already on this row for Owner) lists both Milnor and Gwinner as MDU gas-service towns, consistent with but not naming the route between them, and separately fails url_verifier's name check for this pipeline so is not usable as a second ref. The PN1018 Pipeline News 'Planned Projects' PDF (already on this row for Start) does not mention this project, Montana-Dakota Utilities, or either town anywhere in its extracted text -- checked, not found. No second independent source naming both termini was found this session.

verifications.note: "Bismarck-based Montana Dakota Utilities is building a $13.8 million pipeline to provide natural gas to a South Korea-owned manufacturing facility in southeastern North Dakota ... MDU says construction of the 12-inch, 21-mile long pipeline to the Doosan Bobcat Inc.'s factory in Gwinner will be complete in September 2018."

resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded SegmentCost=13,800,000 USD matches exactly: this AP wire item states MDU 'is building a $13.8 million pipeline' for the Doosan Bobcat facility. Single-source (medium tier) rather than high: the Washington Times piece (also on this row, via Wayback) carries the identical '$13.8 million' figure in identical wording ('Bismarck-based Montana Dakota Utilities is building a $13.8 million pipeline...') -- it is the same AP dispatch republished, not an independent confirmation, per the standing wire-story rule, so it is not counted as a second source here. The wahpetondailynews.com piece (also on this row) discusses only residential/business hookup costs for the later service-extension phase, never a project total, and the PN1018 PDF does not mention this project at all. Also note for context, not a discrepancy: the same AP item separately reports the North Dakota Industrial Commission approved $10.5 million in Bank of North Dakota financing toward the project -- a financing figure, not the total project cost, so it does not conflict with the recorded $13,800,000 SegmentCost.
